binLabels.instruct: To show how to do it

note.text: Owls sleep in the daytime and hunt at night. Their soft feathers help them fly without making a sound.
The sun is a giant ball of hot, glowing gas. It gives our planet light and warmth every day.
Honeybees live together in a busy hive. They turn flower nectar into sweet, golden honey.
Pip the puppy chased his tail round and round. He spun so fast he flopped into the leaves!
A silly frog tried to catch the moon in the pond. He splashed all night, but the moon just winked!
Mabel the cat thought she was a lion. She roared at a feather and pounced on a sock!
To make a paper boat, first fold the paper in half. Next, fold the corners down. Then shape the boat.
To plant a seed, first dig a small hole. Then drop the seed in. Last, give it some water.
To wash your hands, first turn on the water. Next, scrub with soap. Then rinse and dry them.

page_title.en: The Harbor Post — Author's Purpose: Inform, Entertain & Instruct (Grade 2)

page_intro.en: A free interactive Grade 2 reading activity: help Marlow the pelican sort harbor notes by why the author wrote them. Read each short note, then send it to the right bin — to tell facts, to tell a fun story, or to show you how to do something. A friendly first look at the author's purpose. Common Core RI.2.6.
